correctness.rationale: The two conditional laws follow from generator identities for arbitrary antiderivatives of \(x\) and \(z\). Independently, setting \(d=y-x\) and \(F=xd-(c-a)x^2/(2a)\), direct symbolic differentiation gives \(LF=a d^2+(\rho-z)x^2\). Integrating under an invariant measure yields the exact defect identity. Equality forces \(d=0\) and \((\rho-z)x^2=0\) in the support; invariance leaves precisely \((0,0,0)\) and \((\pm\sqrt{b\rho},\pm\sqrt{b\rho},\rho)\). Strict excursion and sign-change conclusions then follow from positivity and zero mean of \(d\).
correctness.risk: As in the Liu record, the theorem constrains compact invariant measures but does not assert existence of a particular chaotic invariant measure.

value.rationale: The exact defect converts the natural nonzero-equilibrium height \(\rho=2c-a\) into a universal stationary excursion law and identifies every zero-defect invariant measure. final_claim: For every compact invariant probability measure of the Chen system \(\dot x=a(y-x),\ \dot y=(c-a)x-xz+cy,\ \dot z=xy-bz\) with \(a,b>0\) and \(\rho=2c-a>0\), one has \(\mathbb E[y\mid x]=x\), \(\mathbb E[xy\mid z]=bz\), and \[\mathbb E[(z-\rho)x^2]=a\mathbb E[(y-x)^2].\] Equality occurs exactly for mixtures of the origin and the two nonzero equilibria; every non-equilibrium compact invariant measure has positive mass above \(z=\rho\) and both signs of \(y-x\).
limitations: No claim is made about uniqueness, mixing or physicality of invariant measures.
